messages:
sasha: Quick FYI — ran an AWQ/INT8 shadow rollout against the summarization eval set with prefix-cache ON + continuous batching. seeing a consistent quality delta when prefix lengths > 128 tokens. rouge-L down ~1.8 and factuality checks failing more often. :frowny:

liam: ugh. which model + quant combo? and what was the batcher config?

sasha: model: redwood/llm-13b-v2 (onboarded yesterday), quant: awq-int8-v2, batcher: continuous with max_batch_size=32, max_latency_ms=80, prefetch enabled, prefix_cache_ttl=600s. shadow run id: run-2056-awq-prefetch-01

anya: can you paste the small trace? interested in cache hit/miss behavior during the long prefixes.

sasha: pasted logs below (trimmed):
```
[2056-03-18 14:03:12] request id=abc123 prefix_len=220 cache_hit=false kv_warmup=true
[2056-03-18 14:03:12] batcher flush id=bf1 size=16 latency=72ms quant=awq-int8-v2
[2056-03-18 14:03:13] kvcache-evict model=llm-13b-v2 reason=staleness ttl=600s
[2056-03-18 14:03:13] quality-check rouge-L delta=-1.8 source=eval-set-a
```

devon: interesting — looks like when the prefix cache TTL is long, the AWQ's per-token reconstruction interacts badly with the prefetch path. prefetched KV blobs might be slightly stale compared to the newly generated KV from FP8 baseline, causing small decoding divergence that compounds on long prefixes.

liam: makes sense. AWQ has a different quantized residual distribution vs GPTQ/FP8, so a mismatch between cached KV (generated under one quant profile) and live KV (served with another path) could amplify errors. Did you try disabling prefetch or lowering TTL?

sasha: yes. quick ablation:
- prefix_cache_ttl=60s -> rouge-L delta -0.6
- prefetch disabled -> rouge-L delta -0.4 but latency p95 increased ~18ms
- batching -> switching to bursty batching (max_batch_size=8) -> p95 down but throughput hit

anya: so tradeoffs: consistency vs latency/throughput. We should codify a per-model quant-aware cache policy. e.g., if quant profile != baseline_fp_format then TTL default = 30s and prefetch disabled, fallback to on-demand.

devon: +1. Another option: mark cached KV with quant-profile metadata and validate on use. If quant_profile mismatch, either rehydrate (recompute with current quant) or skip cached entry. Overhead might be acceptable for long prefixes where quality matters.

liam: storing profile metadata is low-effort, but rehydrate on miss could spike latency. Could we do speculative rehydration in background while serving from cached KV but attach a rerank/fact-check step that rejects outputs if confidence low? complex though.

sasha: initial proposal in the run notes: 1) add quant_profile tag to cache entries 2) default policy: if mismatch and prefix_len>128 -> bypass cache; if mismatch and prefix_len<=128 -> accept cache and schedule async rehydration for next request 3) expose TTL knob per-model in console and include recommended values per quant family (AWQ: 30-60s, GPTQ: 120-300s, FP8: 600s)

bench-bot: Shadow run run-2056-awq-prefetch-01 summary:
- throughput: 420qps (shadow)
- p95 latency: 82ms (prefetch on)
- rouge-L delta vs fp32 baseline: -1.8 (prefix_len>128)
- cache_miss_ratio spiked from 4%->21% during warmup spikes

anya: can we template this into the onboarding checklist? new-model bringup step: "run quant-aware batch/caching matrix" that tests TTLs [30,60,300,600], prefetch on/off, batching modes (continuous/bursty) and record quality/latency tradeoffs.

devon: yep. also add a metric: "kv_profile_mismatch_rate" and alert if >5% during shadow. That will help catch models that are fragile under cached KV reuse.

liam: For immediate mitigation, suggest rolling a canary config: for AWQ/int8 families set prefix_cache_ttl=60s and prefetch=false in production rollout. We'll monitor eval gating.

sasha: I'll open a PR with a small cache-metadata patch + onboarding test harness (tests/quant_cache_matrix.py) and a shadow-run plan. tagging @infra for potential perf impacts.

devon: thanks — ack from me. @sasha add the expected rollback criteria (rouge-L drop >1.0 or p95 increase >25ms) so ops can flip quickly. :thumbsup:

liam: good plan. small nit: add a column for "effective token-cost delta" in the matrix so product teams see cost vs quality tradeoffs when we disable prefetch or lower TTL.

sasha: will do. starting the PR + shadow run 2 with TTL=60, prefetch=false, batching=bursty. ETA 3h.

bench-bot: scheduled shadow run run-2056-awq-prefetch-02 at 2056001800 (ETA 3h).

anya: awesome — ping here when results are in.
